reason_for_version_bump: While CONSTRUCTING the entailment layer (still before any structure.py run on data), rules E6 (inapprox=>decision!=P) and E7 (decision=P=>no approx-hardness) were found INVALID for this atlas: under R1 the approximation charge attaches to the optimization object and the decision charge to the decision object, which can differ. Counterexample XOR-SAT: decision=P (GF(2) feasibility) yet MAX-3LIN is inapprox (Hastad 2001), so the cell (decision=P, approximation=inapprox) is OCCUPIED, not forbidden. E6/E7 (and the FPTAS rule E5) are demoted to informational; only E1 (counting_FP=>decision_P) and E2 (parallel_defined_only_within_P, antecedent tightened to {NPC,harder}) remain column-forbidding. This is a theory correction, not a data-driven edit; per the locking discipline a changed prediction is a new version (v2), not an edit to v1. v1 is retained as the record.
note: Coding, predicted signatures, missingness/measured policies, and kill thresholds are locked BEFORE any structure.py run on real atlas data (R7). Harness debugging uses a synthetic toy table, never the pilot. A changed prediction is a new prereg version, never an edit. The pilot structure preview is a harness sanity-check only; the H1-H3 verdict is A3 on the full ~120-problem atlas.

coding_scheme.principle: Association (Cramer's V) and effective-dimensionality (MCA) treat every charge as CATEGORICAL. No charge is forced onto a numeric axis (I4).
coding_scheme.ordinal_use: Ordinal codings are used ONLY for the human-readable occupancy/gap narrative and an ordinal-vs-categorical sensitivity check; clustering must be robust to swapping categorical for ordinal coding (spec I4 sensitivity).
coding_scheme.sentinels: open / unmeasured / n.a. are first-class categories in the full-table analysis and are NEVER imputed (R2). n.a. (structural) and open (unknown) are distinct categories; collapsing them is forbidden.
coding_scheme.measured: measured / measured-scaling cells are coded identically to their value in the main analysis and removed in the --drop-measured ablation (R9).

H1_dimensionality.prediction: Hardness is a vector: at least 3 effective dimensions; the charges do not collapse onto the decision axis.
H1_dimensionality.decision_rule: H1 SUPPORTED iff, in BOTH the full-table and the complete-case MCA (R4), at least 3 dimensions each exceed the mean eigenvalue (Kaiser-style threshold 1/K over K indicator dimensions). H1 requires agreement across both analyses; disagreement is reported as a sociology-of-study confound, not a hardness finding.
H1_dimensionality.anti_prediction_degeneracy: Prior says degeneracy will NOT fire; the witnesses below already contradict it. The analysis must still be allowed to say it (kill-2).

H2_multiplets.prediction: Problems cluster into recurring charge signatures for structural reasons. Locked witness signatures (theory-driven, before curation):

witness_signatures.permanent_vs_determinant: Same algebraic surface, SAME decision (both P: determinant in P/NC; permanent's 0/1 decision = perfect-matching in P), OPPOSITE counting (determinant FP, permanent #P-complete) and OPPOSITE parallelization (determinant NC, permanent open/RNC). A counting+parallel decoupling at fixed decision.
witness_signatures.vc_vs_clique: Both decision NPC; OPPOSITE approximation (VC APX-complete / 2-approx, CLIQUE inapprox / n^(1-eps)) AND OPPOSITE parameterized (VC FPT by k, CLIQUE W[1] by k). The canonical approximation+parameterized decoupling at fixed decision.
witness_signatures.two_sat_horn_xor: All decision P; 2-SAT and Horn-SAT counting #P-complete while XOR-SAT counting FP (affine); Horn-SAT parallelization P-complete while XOR-SAT/2-SAT parallelization NC. Decision-easy rows that decouple on counting AND parallelization.
witness_signatures.xor_sat: decision P, counting FP, yet MAX-3LIN inapprox, Tseitin proof_size exp, and landscape clustering-OGP-known (random k-XORSAT freezing): a maximally decoupled row. The charge-8-vs-charge-1 and R1 (different-object) witness.
witness_signatures.php_family: proof_size exp in Resolution (Haken 1985) while human-trivial; most other charges n.a. (a fixed unsat family, not a decision problem) -- the charge-6 witness and an R1/R2 illustration.

H3_forbidden_regions.prediction: Some charge combinations are empty and provably MUST be. Locked theorem-forbidden cells (column-expressible entailment rules that survive the R1 object-mismatch scrutiny, R5/R6):
forbidden_cells: (counting=FP, decision in {NPI-candidate,NPC,harder}) -- E1 counting_FP_implies_decision_P (counting the decision's own witnesses in FP decides existence)
(decision in {NPC,harder}, parallelization in {NC,P-complete}) -- E2 parallel_defined_only_within_P (NC subset of P; the within-P charge is n.a. off P)
H3_forbidden_regions.reclassified_informational: E5 (FPTAS needs strongly-NP-hard + poly-bounded objective), E6 (inapprox=>decision!=P), E7 (decision=P=>no approx-hardness) are NOT column-forbidding: each holds only if the two charges refer to the SAME object, which in a charge atlas they generally do not (R1). They are kept as informational rules with their exact preconditions (R6). Predicted OCCUPIED (not forbidden): (decision=P, approximation=inapprox) via XOR-SAT/MAX-3LIN.

missingness_policy.rule: R4 -- run every dimensionality/association analysis twice: (a) full table with sentinels as categories, (b) complete-case sub-block dropping any charge/problem carrying a sentinel. A structure claim (H1 especially) counts only if it holds in BOTH.
missingness_policy.rationale: MCA over many open/n.a. cells can surface an axis that separates well-studied worst-case problems from ensemble-only problems -- a sociology-of-study artifact, not hardness.

measured_policy.rule: R9 -- structure.py runs with and without measured cells (--drop-measured). No H1/H2/H3 claim may rest on measured cells alone; any claim that appears only with measured cells present is reported as measurement-dependent, not established.
measured_policy.v1_scope: Only already-banked experiments fill measured cells (the Census backbone datum). New measurements are separate mini-projects queued from blank cells, not atlas work.

occupancy_policy.rule: R3 -- occupancy, forbidden-region, and gap analysis run over ALL 2-D charge pairs and a PRE-SPECIFIED set of 3-D triples (locked here to prevent post-hoc triple-fishing).
occupancy_policy.gap_definition: An empty cell in an examined marginal that is NOT theorem-forbidden (no column-forbidding entailment rule fires) and has no known inhabitant. Each gap is stated as a falsifiable claim: 'a natural problem with charges (...) should exist; none is known.'

claim_standard.forbidden: A cell called forbidden cites a column-forbidding entailment rule (theorem) or a conjecture; unlabelled empty cells are gaps, not forbidden. Object-dependent rules (E5/E6/E7) never forbid a cell.
claim_standard.surprising_vs_entailed: H1 associations are reported split into entailment-forced (a known theorem links the charges) vs surprising (no known theorem).

kill_thresholds.population_failure_A1: pilot applicable-cell cited coverage < 70% (or uncited-folklore cells remain) -> literature too sparse for a charge table at this standard -> rescope to fewer charges or kill; write the negative note (spec 5.1).
kill_thresholds.degeneracy_A3: effective dimensionality ~= 1: first MCA dimension holds >= 90% of retained inertia AND median off-diagonal Cramer's V >= 0.8, in BOTH full-table and complete-case -> hardness is scalar at this resolution -> write the negative note (spec 5.2).
kill_thresholds.time_box: A1 within two weekend blocks; total attention ceiling 25 h paired; $0 compute (literature + analysis only).
